The basic implementation of a power system is made up of a bunch of smaller system components, each connected to the room/area its associated with, and which are ultimately connected to and managed by the sector in which the room is located. Simple enough, right?

Well, simple things often become more complex when networking is involved. And since we're working on the game with a heavy focus on co-operative multiplayer, everything must be networked. Luckily it isn't rocket surgery though, so I have a good chunk of the power system working as intended, at least in a basic form. I'll be doing some tinkering over the next few days to expand the system a bit and kill some early bugs, but I expect good things. A space station requires a great many things to run, and these things also need power to function. But interesting things happen when systems start to fail, or worse, lose power completely. That is where the best gameplay lies.

I think we also have a fairly unique and interesting idea for an additional gameplay element to do with that, but I'm not ready to share all the details just yet. Something something blown fuses...
